title: N-TORC: Native Tensor Optimizer for Real-Time Constraints
problem: HLS-based compilers achieve lower latency than overlay architectures but have time-consuming compilation and unpredictable area/latency outcomes, making it impractical to simultaneously satisfy latency constraints and minimize area.
motivation: Deploying ML models with predictable real-time guarantees on resource-constrained hardware requires rapid synthesis methods that jointly optimize latency, area, and accuracy.
method: N-TORC learns how each computation layer performs and uses resources by analyzing real data, then tunes these learned patterns to your constraints. A mathematical optimizer (Mixed Integer Program solver) uses these tuned models to rapidly generate hardware designs meeting your latency targets while minimizing area and maintaining model accuracy.
key_novelty: Instead of slow end-to-end hardware compilation, N-TORC combines data-learned performance and area models for each computation layer with mathematical optimization (Mixed Integer Programming) to rapidly generate hardware designs meeting latency requirements.
contributions: Data-driven models for dataflow layer performance and resources with improved accuracy over prior approaches
Framework for generating Pareto-optimal architectures satisfying latency constraints while optimizing accuracy and cost
MIP-based solver achieving 1000X speedup over stochastic search for architecture generation

metrics.accuracy: higher accuracy than prior performance and resource models

limitations: Scalability to larger networks, applicability to diverse workload types, and power/thermal optimization not discussed.
